title: Bertini dimension cut through prescribed closed points in an integral variety
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $\dim X=m$ for an integer $m\geq2$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $F\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set of closed points (each singleton is closed). There exist an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ of dimension $m-1$ and a closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $F\subseteq i(|Y|)$. No smoothness, properness, or quasi-projectivity assumption on $X$ is imposed; $F$ may be empty.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, printed p.4, specialized to algebraically closed k, with Y given its reduced induced structure. Its proof handles arbitrary separated finite-type varieties using Nagata and Chow, before the projective Bertini step. This is the codimension-one theorem, not Corollary 1.9 with y=1.

proof.text: Use the integral Chow envelope over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: write $\pi:P\to X$ for its proper surjection, $P\subset Z\subset\mathbf P^N_k$ for its dense open projective closure, and $U\subset X$ for the nonempty open over which $\pi$ is an isomorphism. The cited envelope gives integral $P,Z$ and proper $Z$. Both are finite type: $Z$ is a closed subscheme of projective space, and $P$ is an open in this Noetherian scheme. The dimension-of-opens lemma, on $X,P,Z$ and the isomorphic opens $U,\pi^{-1}U$, gives $\dim Z=\dim P=\dim X=m$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, Chow paragraph and projective reduction; use the projective closure of the Chow envelope (as in Stacks 0208) to perform the open restriction before taking its proper image.

proof.text: For each $x\in F$, the nonempty closed subset $\pi^{-1}\{x\}$ of $P$ contains a closed point $p_x$ by the Jacobson lemma. Its residue field is $k$ by the closed-point residue lemma. It is also closed in $Z$: the same residue field has transcendence degree zero over $k$, so the closed-point criterion applies in $Z$. Choose, in addition, a closed point $p_0$ of $Z$ in its nonempty open $\pi^{-1}U\subset P\subset Z$, using density of closed points. Set $S=\{p_x:x\in F\}\cup\{p_0\}$. This is a finite nonempty closed set in $Z$, contained in $P$, and $\pi(S)$ contains $F$. This works also for $F=\varnothing$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, choose F prime above F and enlarge F by a point in the birational isomorphism open.

proof.text: Give $S$ its reduced induced closed structure. For $L=\mathcal O_Z(1)$ the projective embedding makes $L$ ample. Choose $n>0$ sufficiently large for the section-generation lemma, and put $M=L^{\otimes n}$ and $V=\ker(\Gamma(Z,M)\to\Gamma(S,M|_S))$. Proper coherent finiteness at $q=0$ makes $\Gamma(Z,M)$, hence $V$, finite-dimensional (an invertible module is locally free of rank one). Every section in $V$ vanishes on $S$, while the cited generation theorem says that $V$ generates $M$ on $Z\setminus S$ and defines an immersion there. Apply the new immersive-system lemma to obtain precisely the codimension-two witness and base-locus bound required for irreducible Bertini.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, infinite-field projective step; Stacks 0FD5 and 0G4F hypotheses (3),(4).

proof.text: The field $k$ is algebraically closed in the function field $k(Z)$: an algebraic element has a minimal polynomial split over $k$, so in a field it equals one of its roots in $k$. The field-extension lemma and generic-point criterion therefore make $Z$ geometrically irreducible. Irreducible Bertini applied to $(Z,M,V)$ gives a nonempty coefficient open $O$ with geometrically irreducible zero schemes. The inclusion $V\hookrightarrow\Gamma(Z,M)$ is nonzero, since its sections generate off the finite set $S$ in dimension $m\ge2$. Intersect $O$ with the nonempty open of coefficients giving nonzero sections. This intersection is nonempty: affine coefficient space is irreducible, as its polynomial coordinate ring is a domain. By the Jacobson and residue lemmas it has a $k$-point. Choose its section $s\ne0$ and write $H=Z(s)$; then $H$ is geometrically irreducible and contains $S$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, classical irreducible Bertini over infinite k; Stacks 037P, 054Q and 0G4F.

proof.text: On each nonempty affine trivializing open in integral $Z$, the nonzero section $s$ is a nonzero element of a domain: restriction to the generic point is injective, and a section zero there is zero on every trivializing affine, hence globally. Thus the zero ideal of $s$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. The local description of zero schemes makes $H$ an effective Cartier divisor. The integral scheme $Z$ has pure dimension $m$ (its only irreducible component is itself), so Cartier purity gives dimension $m-1$ to every component of $H$. There is just one, by the preceding step. Endow $|H|$ with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $D\subset Z$. It is integral and has dimension $m-1$, since reduction leaves the underlying space unchanged. It contains $S$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, dimension m minus one of a hypersurface section, followed by reduced induced structure.

proof.text: Form $E=D\times_Z P=D\cap P$, a closed subscheme of $P$ and a nonempty open subscheme of integral $D$, since it contains $S$. Hence $E$ is integral and $\dim E=m-1$ by the dimension-of-opens lemma. Its closed immersion into $P$ is proper, so the composite $f:E\to P\xrightarrow{\pi}X$ is proper. Consequently $T=f(|E|)$ is closed in $X$. It is irreducible and nonempty: inverse images of two closed subsets covering $T$ cover the irreducible space $E$, so one already contains its whole image. Give $T$ its reduced induced structure $Y\hookrightarrow X$. Then $Y$ is integral and contains $F$, since $S\subset E$ and $\pi(S)\supset F$.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, open restriction and proper image paragraphs, in the reverse order provided by the Chow envelope.

proof.text: The nonempty open $E\cap\pi^{-1}U$ contains $p_0$. Under $\pi^{-1}U\simeq U$ its underlying subset is exactly $T\cap U$: a point of $T\cap U$ has all its preimages over $U$. The reduced induced structures agree there. Indeed, on each affine open of $U$ both are the quotient by the unique radical ideal vanishing on that subset; the uniqueness clause of the reduced-induced-structure theorem supplies the isomorphism. Thus $E\cap\pi^{-1}U\simeq Y\cap U$. Applying dimension-of-opens on integral $E,Y$ yields $\dim Y=\dim E=m-1$. Finally $Y$ is separated and finite type over $k$: on affine opens of the finite-type Noetherian $X$ it is a quotient by an ideal, so is finite type, and its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $X$. This gives all the required clauses without assuming $X$ proper, smooth, or quasi-projective.

source.place: Theorem 1.8, dimension of the image because the chosen subvariety meets the isomorphism open.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 1.8, printed p.4; Chow envelope followed by its projective closure combines the Nagata/Chow reductions, and the infinite-field Bertini step is expanded with Stacks 0FD5, 0G4F. All assembly arguments are written above.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q100-d158a5706 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Charles–Poonen Theorem 1.8 (p.4) and its proof, and Stacks 0G4F and 0FD5 in the source. The item is the theorem for algebraically closed k with every hypothesis kept, and the route matches the source: the integral Chow envelope does the Nagata+Chow work, with p_0 over the isomorphism open U, and the infinite-field Bertini step goes through 0FD5 and 0G4F. All 7 steps check against what the cited nodes state. Step 2 makes the lifted points closed in Z through the closed-point/trdeg node. Step 3 meets 0FD5's hypotheses with Z proper and S reduced, and H^0 is finite-dimensional. Step 4 gets geometric irreducibility from 037P and 054Q, and V≠0. Step 5 uses Cartier purity with m≥2. Steps 6–7 are the proper image and the dimension through the uniqueness of the reduced structure over U. The new node lem-sfb-immersive-finite-base-bertini-conditions is statement-only, self-contained, and true. For (b), the base locus lies in S, and a closed point has codim d≥2. For (a), take a smooth point off S: two ratios recentred at it are regular parameters, which gives one codim-2 component through it that is not in H_{v1}. I tested it on d=2 with a singular cone and on S=∅. It does not duplicate the zl finite-cover nodes, which assume a smooth affine base, and it does not restate a clause of the item. Batch-5 flags: the recomputed closure reaches only def-trf-schematically-dense-open (a definition), lem-trf-local-fibre-ring-dimension-inequality (00OM), lem-trf-affine-open-limit-descent and lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change (both Mathlib leaves). None of these is trace-formula or Poincaré-duality content, so I accept all four flagged citations. I accept the worker's generic tool_uses. I made no changes.
